title: Part 2.III — Act
role: Third Part-2 chapter and the volume's strongest EXEGETICAL anchor to existing corpus indices. Act is the term scholastic realism features as the locus of motive: action-as-actualization (Aristotelian energeia, the bringing-out of dunamis into actuality) is taken as the originating ground that explains both agent and scene. Burke reads Aristotle and Aquinas in tandem (the opening subsection is titled 'Aristotle and Aquinas') and develops a cluster of act-vocabulary: pathetic fallacy (the projection of motive-attributes from agent to scene), incipient and delayed action (acts not yet outwardly executed are still dramatistically real — the closest Burke comes to a phenomenology of intention), the distinction between realist family and nominalist aggregate modes of grouping acts, and a closing 'Psychology of Action' subsection drawing on G. H. Mead's biological-action lineage and the Korzybski general-semantics frame. This is the chapter that directly anchors Aristotle Complete Works + Phantasia Cluster + Bowin AMT cross-pipeline edges; every other Heidegger/Aristotle bridge in the pipeline runs through this chapter's Burke-Aristotle primary engagement.
